description: Unauthorized Modification of Firewall Rules via S3 An attacker could attempt to modify firewall rules by either compromising the S3 bucket directly, intercepting the pipeline process, or exploiting IAM misconfigurations to gain write access to the configuration files. An attacker with access to the AWS environment could modify the firewall rules to create allowed paths for malicious traffic, disable critical security controls, or create backdoors for future access.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1562.007 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Firewall
recommendation: Implement strict S3 bucket policies and access controls
recommendation: Implement change detection and approval workflow

description: Pipeline Service Role Compromise Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM roles, steal credentials, or compromise the build/deploy process to gain the ability to deploy malicious firewall configurations. An attacker compromises a CodeBuild instance and uses the attached role to modify firewall policies, potentially creating security holes in the network infrastructure.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
mitreATT&CK: T1552.005 - Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API
recommendation: Implement least privilege IAM policies

mitreATT&CK: T1562.008 - Impair Defenses: Disable Cloud Logs

description: DDoS Attack Against Network Firewall Attackers could generate large volumes of traffic through the spoke VPCs or exploit the centralized nature of the inspection architecture to overwhelm the Network Firewall's capacity. An attacker generates a high volume of traffic from compromised resources in spoke VPCs, causing the Network Firewall to become overwhelmed and impacting legitimate traffic flow.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service

description: Cross-AZ Man-in-the-Middle Attack Attackers could attempt to intercept traffic between availability zones by exploiting routing misconfigurations or compromising network components. An attacker compromises a resource in one AZ and exploits routing or firewall failover mechanisms to intercept traffic destined for another AZ.

description: Transit Gateway Quota Exhaustion Attackers could create numerous VPC attachments or generate excessive connection requests to exhaust Transit Gateway quotas and capacity. An attacker with appropriate permissions creates multiple VPC attachments or generates high volumes of connection requests until reaching service quotas.

mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement quota monitoring and alerting

description: Firewall Bypass During AZ Failover During AZ failover events, there might be brief periods where traffic routing is reconfigured, potentially creating opportunities for traffic to bypass firewall inspection. An attacker monitors for AZ failures or triggers failover events, then attempts to send malicious traffic during the transition period.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1562.007 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Firewall
